I cannot perform a local network scan as the `nmap` tool is not found. Also, the `hostname` command is not available to directly get the IP address. However, I was able to retrieve the IP address `10.88.0.3/16` from `ip a`.

To proceed, please ensure `nmap` is installed or provide an alternative method for network scanning.
install tool nmap and scan local network and give me report in tabel

Nmap is not installed. To install it, run:
`sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install nmap`

Once installed, you can scan your local network. Assuming your local network is 192.168.1.0/24, the command would be:
`nmap -sV 192.168.1.0/24`

This command performs a service version detection scan (-sV) on the specified network range. The output will list active hosts and their open ports and services, which can then be formatted into a table.
